newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares at record levels in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares at record levels in bourse trade.

text.p: German shares traded at record levels in bourse trade on Monday, with the blue-chip DAX index lifted by a nearly one-percent rise on Wall Street on Friday and the continued support of a firm dollar.

The DAX index was up 18.91 points, or 0.51 percent, at 3,763.35 points in early trade, having earlier hit a new all-time high of 3,770.90 points. The June DAX future contract, which expires this week, was up 17 points at 3,766.

"Basically there isn't a whole lot around to talk about this morning. We're higher on the back of Wall Street and we could reach 3,800 points during bourse trade. Turnover is very thin," a Frankfurt broker said.

The Dow Jones Industrial index of U.S. stocks ended trade on Friday up 70.57 points at 7,782.04 points, a rise of nearly one percent, after another rampant week in Wall Street's greatest bull-run in history.
The Dow Jones industrial average has gained 1,000 points in just a little over a month after portfolio managers have ploughed fresh cash into stocks.

The rise on Friday came after a larger-than-expected drop in May wholesale prices. Analysts in the U.S. are expecting Tuesday's release of May consumer prices to further reinforce optimism in domestic financial markets.
This is expected to feed further gains for the German stock market, which has been following the U.S. index slavishly in recent weeks.
The markets were also looking to the EU summit in Amsterdam, where it was hoped that an agreement on a stability pact would help further stabilise market worries about the future of currency union.
The strong dollar helped lift chemical stocks early on, but in bourse trade this sector was prone to profit-taking.
Degussa AG was down 60 pfennigs at 94 marks, while Merck KGaA was down 30 pfennigs at 74.70 marks.
Bayer AG was up 53 pfennigs at 67.78 marks, having fallen in pre-bourse electronic trade.
